name: Luis Soto
life: “I still remember my first supervisor asking a question that wasn't quite a question.” On Thursday, near the window at Night Shift Donuts, Luis knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I was a probationer then. I kept quiet because the man signing the note was my mentor.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a red windbreaker and a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. Luis has fine brows over wide-set eyes, with brown hair pinned away from the temples. Luis starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak during a conversation.
personality: Luis thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Luis sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To correct the old supervisor's mistake openly.
family: Iris Vidal is Luis’s stepsibling. Luis asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Iris remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *A ship without postcards*, Iris says, “I am saving the crooked rail that proves my photograph was taken on the early shift.”
connections: Jo Grant (department colleague). A caption writer and the colleague who stayed silent both have something specific to correct.

reactions.situation: The shopkeeper asks for a public correction
reactions.response: Luis agrees a place and size for the correction with the person who was named.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Luis asks the nearest shop worker to stay too, then talks about ordinary things until the child can explain who is late.

reactions.situation: When family demands an immediate answer
reactions.response: Luis asks them to walk to the corner together and listen until the corner comes.
